text.en: Raju saw a family receiving free rice at a ration shop. "Why is that?" he asked.

Food security means reliable access to enough safe and nutritious food for an active, healthy life. Availability describes the supply. Access means people can actually obtain food. Utilisation concerns diet, safe water and how the body uses nutrients. Stability means these conditions continue over time.
Fair price shops distribute food through the Public Distribution System. The Food Corporation of India helps procure, store and move grain. Buffer stocks can help maintain supplies during shortages. The National Food Security Act of 2013 provides food and nutritional entitlements for eligible groups. Tamil Nadu’s broad PDS and school meal programmes address different needs.
Food quantity alone does not ensure good nutrition. Dietary variety, food safety, clean water, care and health services can all matter.
Food security means that all people have enough safe and nutritious food at all times.

text.en: Food security involves availability, access and good use of food. These conditions need to remain stable over time.

board.text: PDS

text.en: Poverty, droughts and rising prices threaten it.

board.text: buffer stock

text.en: The Public Distribution System makes grain and other notified supplies available through fair price shops. The Food Corporation of India helps procure, store and move grain and maintain buffer stocks.

board.text: ration shop

text.en: The National Food Security Act of twenty thirteen establishes food grain and nutrition entitlements for eligible groups. It covers more than just grain distribution.

board.text: malnutrition

text.en: Tamil Nadu uses a broad public distribution system and has a long-running school meal programme. The two address different parts of food security.

board.text: National Food Security Act

text.en: A varied diet supplies energy, protein, vitamins and minerals. These support health, and nutrition is also affected by safe water, care and other conditions.

board.text: food security

text.en: Food can come from local harvests, trade or stored stocks. This dimension asks whether enough food is available in a place.

board.text: Availability means enough food is supplied

text.en: Food may be nearby yet unaffordable. Access can also depend on travel, transport and how a household receives supplies.

board.text: Access asks whether people can obtain food

text.en: Even when the amount of food in markets is unchanged, a loss of wages or increase in prices can make it harder to buy enough.

board.text: Purchasing power links income and prices

text.en: Available food needs to be safe and provide needed nutrients. Clean water, sanitation and care affect how well people can use those nutrients.

board.text: Utilisation includes diet and health conditions

text.en: A household may have adequate food after harvest and struggle a few months later. Food security needs reliable access throughout the year.

board.text: Stability means these conditions last

text.en: Farm work or food supplies can vary by season. Some households face repeated periods when income falls or food costs rise.

board.text: Seasonal hardship can occur even with an annual harvest

text.en: A drought may reduce harvests. A flood can also interrupt transport, so food may not reach people even if supplies exist elsewhere.

board.text: Drought and flood affect different parts of the system

text.en: Irrigation, storage and support for farming can increase or stabilise supply. Their effects depend on local conditions and how the programmes work.

board.text: Production policy can influence the food supply

text.en: A support price states a purchase price for selected crops under a policy. Procurement is the actual purchase and collection of grain through public agencies.

board.text: Support prices and procurement are distinct

text.en: Grain can be stored after it is purchased and released later. Good storage and transport help maintain usable supplies.

board.text: Grain stores link harvest and later demand

text.en: A reserve can be drawn on when regular supplies are interrupted. It also needs replenishing, care in storage and a way to reach households.

board.text: Buffer stocks can cushion some shortages

text.en: Grain moves from storage and supply networks through public agencies to shops. Households receive supplies under programme rules.

board.text: Fair price shops are a distribution point

text.en: The national food security law includes provision for eligible households and nutritional support for groups such as children and pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

board.text: Food grain and nutritional entitlements both matter

text.en: The textbook describes Tamil Nadu’s universal public distribution system. Its fair price shops help make supplies available closer to families.

board.text: Tamil Nadu has a broad public distribution approach

text.en: A prepared school meal can support nutrition during the school day. It complements other food supplied or prepared at home.

board.text: School meals address another need

text.en: Imagine a family with access to a market but insufficient income, and another isolated by a flooded road. Both face access problems, for different reasons.

board.text: Food insecurity has more than one cause

text.en: Grains can supply energy, and pulses or other protein foods help provide materials for growth and repair. Vegetables and fruit add fibre and micronutrients.

board.text: A varied diet has different roles

text.en: The body needs vitamins and minerals in smaller amounts than major nutrients. They still play important roles in growth and health.

board.text: Micronutrients are needed in small amounts

text.en: A person can receive enough energy but still lack important nutrients if their diet offers little variety.

board.text: Enough calories may not mean enough nutrition

text.en: It can involve too little energy or nutrients, a lack of some micronutrients, or excess energy intake. Different forms can occur in the same community.

board.text: Malnutrition describes several imbalances

text.en: It can reflect long-term effects of undernutrition, repeated illness and other conditions. One short-term meal change does not explain every case.

board.text: Stunting describes low height for age

text.en: Better storage can strengthen supply, a reachable shop can improve access and a varied school meal can support nutrition. Reliable service helps all three over time.

board.text: Food policy can support several dimensions together

text.en: Check stocks for availability, prices and travel for access, variety and safety for utilisation, and changes between seasons for stability.

problem.en: A flood prevents regular food deliveries. What can a reserve grain stock do, and what else is needed?

text.en: A reserve can supplement the interrupted supply.

why.en: Stored stock can be released when needed.

text.en: Transport and distribution must still reach households.

why.en: A reserve helps availability, while the route to households affects access.

problem.en: Why is eating enough grain different from having a varied diet?

text.en: Grain can provide energy and some nutrients.

why.en: Energy is one part of nutrition.

text.en: Different foods supply additional proteins, vitamins and minerals.

why.en: Dietary variety can help meet different nutritional needs.

requiredIdeas.en: It needs enough nutritious food for all.

points.en: Food security involves availability, access, utilisation and stability.
